shardDecision: Delegated nothing. The slice printer gives two files and 91 changed lines since the commit review 2 judged — one shard by its own sizing, and a two-file slice handed to a child is a round trip that measures nothing. I read both myself: the diff since 024f16d, the whole current `.time-off-calendar` block of globals.css (855-1060), and the whole of TC-03-E2E-11/12/13 plus the helpers they were given (firstOfferedDay, midMonthDay, pageToDay, addDays). The three parts no child can hold I ran over the WHOLE change rather than the slice — the requirement enumeration from the document's own list, the boundary pairs, and blast radius — and to settle the fix's mechanism I read the CSS Grid track-sizing rules against the code rather than taking the commit message's word for it. Reading the sizing question out of the slice's two files is also what let me check the two shipped consequences the fix has (the Month window at a desktop viewport, the Week window's fr division), which is where this pass's one new note came from.

findings.rule: REQ-03-014 with REQ-03-018 — a floor on every day column, and a scroll once the floors exceed the space — read against Edge case 13, which speaks only of 'a 92-day range on a narrow viewport'
findings.claim: the fix is right and the geometry is now the one the rule describes, and the consequence the document never states is that the SHIPPED Month window scrolls at a desktop viewport: 32px times 28-31 days plus the name column is wider than the content well at 1280px, so every reader of a month now gets a horizontal scrollbar where they previously saw the whole month compressed

witness.detail: REQ-03-014 puts the floor on every day column 'WHILE the grid is drawn' — not only under Range — and REQ-03-018 makes the scroll follow from the floors exceeding the space. With --day-col-min: 32px (globals.css:885) and --name-col: 264px, a 30-day month needs 264 + 30*32 = 1224px, while AppShell gives 1280 - 290 (rail) - 2*25 (well padding, AppShell.tsx:89) = ~940px of content: the Month window scrolls at every viewport this product supports, all year — February's 28 days still need 1160px. It is Month alone: 2 weeks needs 264 + 14*32 = 712px and Week 488px, both inside the well. Before this change the same month divided the page into ~22px columns and did not scroll. Both readings are defensible and the code takes the one the requirements state literally; the shipped case now asserts it (e2e/tests/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:813-816). What is worth a person's eye is that the document's only picture of the scroll is Edge case 13's 'narrow viewport' and cases.md's 'A 92-day range is 92 columns and scrolls' Known Gap, neither of which mentions the default window on a desktop — so the value of --day-col-min, chosen for the two-line header, is what silently decides whether a month fits, and nothing in the bundle records that trade.

findings.suggestedFix: Nothing in code — the requirements say what the code does. For the person: record that the floor makes the Month window scroll at a desktop viewport, and if that is unwanted, the next document decides it explicitly (a smaller floor for the presets, or a rule that the floor applies only where the window cannot fit).

dismissed: Review 2's blocker (L1, `min-width: max-content` sizing every day column by the widest header) — CLOSED, checked against its own witness rather than against the commit message. globals.css:1004 now reads `min-width: min-content`, and that is the sum of the floors, not the content: under a min-content constraint CSS Grid §12.6 makes the free space zero and §12.7 makes the used flex fraction zero, so each `minmax(var(--day-col-min), 1fr)` track stays at its base size — and the base size of a track whose MIN sizing function is fixed (32px) is never grown by an item's contribution, because §12.5 grows only tracks with an intrinsic min sizing function. The row's min-content is therefore exactly `--name-col + N * --day-col-min`, which is what the rule's own comment and REQ-03-018 both say. The witness's own state is now a shipped case: TC-03-E2E-13 seeds 'Company Day' as a whole-view holiday in the month the screen opens on (e2e:768-777), asserts the holiday IS drawn in its header, and then asserts every `calendar-day-header-*` box is within half a pixel of the declared floor and that the container's scrollWidth is at most `nameCol + monthDays * floor + 2`. Under the max-content the finding described those two assertions read ~87px and ~2900px and both fail, so the case detects the regression rather than describing it.

Review 1's blocker (the sticky member column pinned to the wrong scrollport) — still closed, re-checked in the current file. `.time-off-calendar-grid` (globals.css:990-1005) now carries `min-width` alone; the border, radius, background and the clipping live on `.time-off-calendar-scroll` (:983-988), which is the box with `overflow-x: auto` and therefore the nearest scrollport ancestor of `.time-off-calendar-who` (:1019-1029). Nothing between them establishes a scrollport — `.time-off-calendar-row` is `display: grid; position: relative` with no overflow. TC-03-E2E-13:876-897 still sets `scrollLeft = 400`, asserts the container moved, and asserts the name cell is within a pixel of the container's left edge.

The new Month assertions are not flaky arithmetic. At the 1280x900 viewport the case sets, AppShell gives a 290px rail and var(--space-9) padding either side (AppShell.tsx:89), so the well is ~940px; the smallest month needs 264 + 28*32 = 1160px and the largest 1256px, so `scrollWidth > clientWidth` holds in every month of the year, and the Week window's 264 + 7*32 = 488px is far inside the well, so its `width > floor` holds too. Neither assertion sits near its boundary.

`midMonthDay()` cannot drift a month away from the screen. `signupOrg` sends no timezone and signup leaves it null (helpers.ts:764-766); `timeOffCalendarToday(null)` resolves through `todayInTimeZone`, which falls back to 'UTC' (requests.ts:640). The screen's today and the helper's `getUTCMonth()` are therefore the same clock, and the 15th is inside whatever month that is.

The Month window now scrolling at a desktop viewport is not CR-32 on its own — REQ-03-014 puts the floor on every day column while the grid is drawn, not only under Range, and REQ-03-018 makes the scroll follow. Carried to the person as note L10 because the document never pictures that consequence.

The moved `background: var(--surface-page)` and the loss of `overflow: hidden` on the grid change no assertion in the suite: the only computed-style reads are a day header's backgroundColor (e2e:83) and two custom properties (e2e:789), and a background on an ancestor does not enter either.

A stale grid drawn beneath the error banner when a 422 answers a scope change — accepted for the same reason review 1 accepted it: contracts §UI Description, row 'Error', puts the banner "above the grid", and time-off/01's REQ-01-049 (specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.md:207-215) is about moving the WINDOW, which the `isCurrentWindow` guard still holds. No document asks for the rows to be cleared on a scope refusal.
The `--day-col-min: 32px` literal is declared, not improvised: cases.md §DS gaps carries it as a named gap with the value's reason, which is the route CLAUDE.md prescribes (CR-11).

CR-26 on the new assertions — none of them is a tautology. `toBeCloseTo(floor, 0)` fails at ~87px under the old CSS; `scrollWidth <= nameCol + days*floor + 2` fails at ~2900px; the Week `width > floor` fails if the floor were ever made a fixed width instead of a minimum. And the `xs` equality for `calendar-today` can fail, because PageHeader lays its action block out with `justify-content: space-between` (PageHeader.tsx:28) and the label is the last flex child — a label wider than `--range-col` moves the buttons left, which is the defect BUG-013 filed.

CR-01/CR-02/CR-03/CR-06 — the route's guards and scoping are untouched; `resolveRows` still filters on `caller.organizationId`, which comes from the session, and the controller is not in the diff. The widened default resolves to the set the `all` scope already answered for the same roles.
CR-04 — no new authorization code; `seedMemberships` writes `role: 'user'` into a String column and its rows are listed, never used to authorize.
CR-21/CR-22 — no migration and no schema change.
CR-10 — no route handler and no server action; the one fetch keeps `credentials: 'same-origin'`.

CR-24/CR-25 — the rewritten TC-01-INT-06/08 and TC-01-E2E-03/11 each replace a refusal assertion the spec withdrew (REQ-03-003) with the positive assertion that replaces it, and the integration pair now seeds a second member so the 200 has a set to be equal to rather than a length to be at least.
CR-28 — no test in the diff pins a port or names devscribed_dev; the new fixture uses setViewportSize and the suite's own helpers.

CR-31 — `maxSpanDays` is optional and the three shipped DateRangePicker consumers pass nothing; the CSS touched is scoped to `.time-off-calendar*`, which nothing outside this screen carries; `TimeOffCalendarWindow` is unwidened and its two anchor functions are untouched; the deleted validation exports have no remaining consumer in apps, packages, e2e or dist.

The branch carries the spec's work and nothing else — `git diff --stat` over the base is exactly the nine files the handoff names, and the two commits since review 2 touch only globals.css and the e2e case.
